operators.O: specialize: z -> (1-theta)*z
integrate over theta from 0 to 1: u(z)=int_0^1 F(theta,z) dtheta

hypotheses.reconstruction_rule: Apply G0001 with z replaced by (1-theta)*z to form F(theta,z), then integrate over theta in [0,1] to obtain G0002.
required_assumptions: z is complex (entire continuation); the z != 0 quotient form is used for G0002, G0003, G0004
integral parameter theta ranges over the compact interval [0, 1]
hypotheses.rationale: The target is the integral of the entire exponential kernel evaluated along the affine parameter path (1-theta)z, which is the k=1 integral form of the exponential-integrator family.

hypotheses.latent_object: F(k,z)=exp(z) if k=0; F(k,z)=(F(k-1,z)-F(k-1,0))/z for k>=1 and z!=0; F(k,0)=1/k!

operators.O: base: F(0,z)=exp(z)
apply recurrence R once to F(0,z)
apply recurrence R twice to F(0,z)
apply recurrence R three times to F(0,z)
evaluate F(0,z) at z=0: F(0,0)=1
evaluate F(2,z) at z=0: F(2,0)=1/2

hypotheses.reconstruction_rule: Start with F(0,z)=G0001. Define recurrence R: F(k,z)=(F(k-1,z)-F(k-1,0))/z for z!=0, with entire extension F(k,0)=1/k!. Apply R once for G0002, twice for G0003, three times for G0004. G0005 is F(0,0), and G0006 is F(2,0).
required_assumptions: z is complex (entire continuation); the z != 0 quotient form is used for G0002, G0003, G0004
each u_k defined below extends to an entire function with u_k(0)=1/k!
hypotheses.rationale: The catalog expressions are consecutive divided-difference quotients generated from exp(z) by subtracting the previous value at z=0 and dividing by z, matching the recurrence definition for the exponential-integrator family.
